mechanisms.name: Word-family substitution
mechanisms.description: A word is replaced by a derivative of the same root across parts of speech: confidence becomes confident or confidently; vary becomes various, variety or a variety of.

mechanisms.name: Cross-part-of speech equivalence
mechanisms.description: Words of different parts of speech stand in for each other on the strength of meaning alone: an adjective such as essential can surface as the modal must or have to, the verb require or the noun necessity.

mechanisms.name: Affirmation and negation
mechanisms.description: A positive formulation is replaced by the negation of its opposite: surprising is heard as not realise or didn't expect that; lack as not enough.

mechanisms.name: Hypernym and hyponym
mechanisms.description: A general term is replaced by a specific instance of it, or the reverse: color becomes red; animal becomes tiger.

mechanisms.name: Abstract and concrete
mechanisms.description: An abstract notion is replaced by the concrete activity that instantiates it: recreation becomes singing and dancing.
